title: The Holy Name of Mary (12 September)
hookLine: a feast of her name, restored in 2002

cards: "And the virgin's name was Mary." Luke saves it for the end of the sentence. First the angel, Gabriel.
Then the town, Nazareth. Then the man she is promised to, Joseph, of the house of David. And then, last, almost quietly, her name.
Today the Church gives a whole feast to that last word. Not to something Mary did, or a moment in her life. Just to her name.
It's also the end of a week of saints, so there's a look back at them, too.

teach.h: MOSES'S SISTER, WHO SANG BY THE SEA.
teach.b: Start with the name itself. It's an old name. In the Douay-Rheims, Moses's sister, who sang by the sea, carries it too: "Mary the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand."
So the girl in Nazareth carried a name that was already old, a name with a song in it. What does it mean? Readers over the centuries have offered guesses.
Luke doesn't say. Second, who says her name. In Luke the angel's greeting is "Hail, full of grace," with no name at all.
A moment later, when she's troubled, he says it: "Fear not, Mary, for thou hast found grace with God." Her name arrives with comfort. Third, why a feast for a name.

teach.h: A NAME STANDS FOR THE PERSON.
teach.b: Catholics hear a name as standing for the whole person. The Church already honors the Holy Name of Jesus, and this feast does the same for his mother: for Catholics, to say her name with love is to turn toward her.
In the Hail Mary, they put her name back into the angel's greeting. This feast has been on the Church's general calendar, off it for a time, and back again.
And now, the week. Stephen of Hungary, and the holy crown.

teach.h: AND THE VIRGIN'S NAME WAS MARY.
teach.b: The Queenship of Mary, queen and mother. Bartholomew, without guile. Joseph Calasanz, and his free schools.
John the Baptist, whose truth cost his head. Jeanne Jugan, for the old. And today, one name.

how: Catholics may keep the optional memorial of the Most Holy Name of Mary on 12 September, and honor her name whenever they pray the Hail Mary, which joins the angel's greeting to her name.

practice: On an out-breath, say her name once, aloud or inside, Mary, then let it rest and breathe a few times before you say it again, adding nothing.
If you pray, pray the Hail Mary slowly and pause where her name comes; if you don't, think of how your own name sounds when someone who loves you says it, and let that be enough.
